articles.title_original: Eight killed in Peruvian military helicopter crash
articles.title_zh: Eight killed in Peruvian military helicopter crash
facts_zh:
Eight killed in Peruvian military helicopter crash
- Published
Eight military personnel have been killed in a helicopter crash in a remote area of Peru known for growing and trafficking drugs.

Authorities say the aircraft came down near the town of Sanabamba during a mission to evacuate an army patrol in the valley of the Apurimac, Ene, and Mantaro rivers, known by its Spanish acronym VRAEM.
Often referred to as 'Cocaine Valley', the area is Peru's largest coca-growing valley where gangs and the remnants of the former Shining Path rebel group operate.

all_titles.en: Eight killed in Peruvian military helicopter crash

articles.title_zh: Turkish officials 'destroyed' pro-opposition TV channel, owner tells BBC
facts_zh:
Turkish officials 'destroyed' pro-opposition TV channel, owner tells BBC
- Published
Turkish authorities have "destroyed" one of the country's most-watched news channels, its London-based owner has told the BBC.
Speaking to the BBC's Newshour, Cafer Mahiroğlu said that nine people connected to Halk TV were arrested this week on charges including money laundering, bribery and spreading misleading information.

Mahiroğlu said that several of his family members were among those arrested when the pro-opposition channel was taken into government control last month, adding that the allegations against him and Halk TV are "completely wrong".

articles.title_zh: 'Poison seller' Kenneth Law apologises in court to the families of his victims
facts_zh:
'Poison seller' Kenneth Law apologises in court to the families of his victims
- Published
The Canadian man who sold toxic chemicals through online suicide forums in 40 countries apologised in court to the families of the victims, saying he deeply regrets his actions and will never repeat them.
Kenneth Law made the remarks on Friday during a sentencing hearing where prosecutors asked a judge to give him a 25-year prison term.

The 61-year-old pleaded guilty in May to 14 counts of aiding the suicide deaths of 14 people in Ontario, Canada, though he has admitted to causing the deaths of dozens of victims in England and Wales.

articles.title_zh: Spanish PM and rivals rally supporters in final pitch for votes
facts_zh:
Spanish PM and rivals rally supporters in final pitch for votes
- Published
Spain's main party leaders have held their final rallies ahead of Sunday's election, with Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez saying he is confident of defying the polls.
"I cannot imagine us losing," he said, posing for selfies with supporters in red T-shirts and accusing conservative rival Alberto Núñez Feijóo of planning a coalition with the far right.

Feijóo's People's Party (PP) is narrowly ahead in the polls, and in the final hours of the campaign he travelled first to Barcelona and then Seville, promising voters a new political era of "truth, decency and good governance".

all_titles.en: Spanish PM and rivals rally supporters in final pitch for votes

Elizabeth May, a Canadian Green party member, originally opened the petition for signatures in July 2026 after a woman from Calgary sponsored it.
The petition requests that the Canadian government declare Hoekstra “persona non grata” due to his “US” diplomatic interference in Canadian domestic affairs”.

articles.title_zh: Kenyan doomsday cult leader convicted over further 123 deaths
facts_zh:
Kenyan doomsday cult leader convicted over further 123 deaths
- Published
A court in Kenya has convicted the leader of a doomsday Christian cult of the manslaughter of 123 of his followers.
Paul Mackenzie was found guilty in Mombasa of ordering his followers, all adults, to fast to death in Shakahola forest near the coast between January 2021 and September 2023.
Earlier this month Mackenzie was jailed for 200 years for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children, in the same mass killing.

articles.title_original: Rare turtles found inside baggage at Amsterdam airport
articles.title_zh: Rare turtles found inside baggage at Amsterdam airport
facts_zh:
Rare turtles found inside baggage at Amsterdam airport
- Published
Twenty-six "very rare" turtles have been seized from a traveller's checked baggage at Amsterdam's Schiphol airport, a Dutch government agency has said.

The Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority (NVWA) said a man flying from Mexico to Hong Kong via the airport was arrested on Saturday after the Vallarta mud turtles were found by customs officers.
The endangered species, thought to be the smallest freshwater turtles in the world with a maximum length of about 10cm (4in), were wrapped in duct tape to prevent them from moving.

all_titles.en: Rare turtles found inside baggage at Amsterdam airport

articles.title_zh: Ex-media executive admits saying Australian child sex abuse survivor 'looking to be raped again'
facts_zh:
Ex-media executive admits saying Australian child sex abuse survivor 'looking to be raped again'
- Published
An Australian former media executive has admitted he said a child sex abuse survivor and prominent advocate "must be looking to be raped again" because of the way she was dressed at an event.
Grace Tame, 31, was groomed and abused by a teacher and has been honoured as Australian of the Year in 2021 for her advocacy work on child safety.
In an op-ed for independent media outlet Crikey, Tame said she overheard Matt Handbury speaking to a friend, and was left distressed by the remark and the failure of others who heard it to intervene.

all_titles.en: Ex-media executive admits saying Australian child sex abuse survivor 'looking to be raped again'

articles.title_original: Millions of wives in South Asia unprotected from marital rape - study
articles.title_zh: Millions of wives in South Asia unprotected from marital rape - study
facts_zh:
Millions of wives in South Asia unprotected from marital rape - study
- Published
Failure to fully criminalise marital rape leaves millions of women and girls unprotected in eight South Asian countries, where intimate partner violence is 35% higher than the global average, says a new study.
More than 100 countries have outlawed marital rape, but a large part of South Asia - India, Afghanistan, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh - remain among the three dozen countries which haven't.
The only South Asian country where rape within marriage attracts the same penalty as any other rape is The Maldives.

all_titles.en: Millions of wives in South Asia unprotected from marital rape - study
